title: The role of color expertise in color preference: Evidence from color naming ability
abstract: Expertise can shape how aesthetic stimuli are perceived and interpreted, but its role in color preference remains unclear. The present study examined whether color expertise and color naming ability are associated with preferences for individual colors. An independent color-name generation stage was first conducted to select non-basic and specialized color terms for stimulus development. Seventy-five participants with different artistic backgrounds then completed a color-preference rating task, a three-alternative forced-choice color-naming task, and a color expertise questionnaire. Greater expertise was associated with more accurate selection of intended color labels, indicating that expertise improved identification of specialized color terms. However, neither expertise nor naming accuracy was significantly associated with color preference. Instead, preference ratings were more closely summarized by the perceptual properties of the stimuli. These findings help distinguish perceptual, linguistic, and experiential influences on color preference by showing that expertise improved color identification but did not systematically alter color liking.
